app.name: Aurora Retail
app.description: Sales administration of the Aurora stores, built with Midnight Indigo: UI and Next.js.

kpis.label: Key figures

header.title: Orders
header.description: Every order of the year. Sort by a column, filter by status and region, or search by customer, store or number.

listing.title: All orders
listing.caption: All orders
listing.noResultsDescription: Search for another term, or clear the filters to see every order.

stores.title: Revenue by store

colors.invalid: Enter a color in the format #RRGGBB or #RGB.
colors.reset: Restore the colors of the build

preview.title: Preview

export.copyFailed: The theme could not be copied. Select the text and copy it instead.

notFound.title: Page not found

search.title: Search icons

results.emptyDescription: Try other words, or search every set and license.

details.attribution: Its license (CC BY 4.0) requires crediting the author: keep the attribution page or ICON-NOTICES.md in your application.
details.palette: Multicolor icon: it keeps its own colors instead of following the text color.
details.intents: In the text color of each intent

snippets.dataDescription: Works in Server and Client Components; only this icon reaches the bundle.

snippets.copyFailed: The code could not be copied. Select it and copy it by hand.

header.title: Icon attribution
header.description: Authors and licenses of the icon sets the application ships. The sets under CC BY 4.0 require this credit.

attributed.one: {{count, number}} set that requires attribution (CC BY 4.0)
attributed.other: {{count, number}} sets that require attribution (CC BY 4.0)

header.title: Components
header.description: Every component of the library, with its variants, a playground, examples with their code and its props.

playground.required: Required: the preview and the code keep the initial value.

api.caption: Props of {{component}}
api.native: Attribute of the native element, passed on unchanged.
api.nativeOnly: `{{component}}` has no props of its own: it takes the attributes of its native element.

button.summary: Action with a visible text label.
button.description: Use it for actions inside the page: saving, confirming, opening a dialog. Mark the main action of a view with the `official` intent; to go to another page, use a `Link`.

actions.title: Actions of a form
actions.description: One `official` solid button for the main action; the others stay soft or ghost.

loading.title: Operation in progress
loading.description: `loading` keeps the label, the look and the focus while the action runs, and tells assistive technologies that the button is busy.

accessibility.name: The visible label is the accessible name; for a button with only an icon, use `IconButton`.
accessibility.type: It is a native button with `type="button"`; pass `type="submit"` in forms.
accessibility.loading: `loading` sets `aria-busy` and ignores activation without taking the focus away; `disabled` means the action is unavailable.

iconButton.summary: Action shown only as an icon, named by a required label.
iconButton.description: Use it where space is short and the icon is well known: a toolbar, the actions of a row, the controls of a player. The `label` says what the action does; when the icon alone is not obvious, use a `Button` with `startIcon`.

actions.title: Actions of a row
actions.description: Ghost icon buttons, each one named after the action and the item it acts on; `error` marks the destructive one.

playback.title: Player controls
playback.description: A large solid button for the main action, whose `label` follows the action it performs next.

accessibility.name: `label` is the accessible name (`aria-label`) and cannot be blank: name the action, e.g. `Remove Spike Spiegel`, not the icon.
accessibility.icon: The icon is hidden from assistive technologies; mark it `decorative`.
accessibility.target: Every size is a square of at least 32 px, above the WCAG 2.2 minimum target.

copyButton.summary: Copies a text to the clipboard and confirms it.
copyButton.description: Put it next to a value the reader will paste elsewhere: a code, a key, a link. `value` can be a function, called at the moment of the copy.

inline.title: Next to a value
inline.description: The icon alone, named by `label` after what it copies.

invite.title: With its name
invite.description: `showLabel` shows the name next to the icon, for a copy that is the main action of its area.

accessibility.name: Name it after what it copies, e.g. `Copy invite link`; the name never changes under the focus.
accessibility.announcement: The result (`Copied`, or `Could not copy`) is announced by a live region and shown by the icon and the intent, not by the color alone.
accessibility.clipboard: The Clipboard API needs a secure context (HTTPS or `localhost`); elsewhere the copy fails and says so.

code.summary: Short code inside running text: a name, a value, a command.
code.description: A `code` element in the monospace font, with the size of the text around it, so it fits a sentence, a heading or a caption alike. For several lines, use `CodeBlock`.

sentence.title: In a sentence
sentence.description: The commands and outputs the reader types or looks for, inside the instructions that explain them.

settings.title: Names and values
settings.description: The name of each setting and its value, in a list that describes them.

accessibility.text: Screen readers read it as plain text: let the sentence tell what it is, e.g. “run the command”.
accessibility.block: For several lines, use `CodeBlock`: a named group that the keyboard can scroll.
accessibility.wrap: A long value breaks anywhere instead of overflowing, so the page never scrolls sideways on a small screen.

codeBlock.summary: Block of source code, colored, with a copy button and one tab per file.
codeBlock.description: Color the code with `highlightCode` on the server (or at build time) and give its result to `code`: the browser receives only the tokens, never the highlighter. A string is shown without colors. `showLineNumbers` numbers the lines and `highlightedLines` marks some of them; `files` shows several files, one tab each.

highlighted.title: Colored on the server
highlighted.description: An async Server Component awaits `highlightCode`; `showLineNumbers` and `highlightedLines` point the reader to the line that matters.

files.title: Several files
files.description: `files` gives each file a tab, and the copy button copies the file shown.

accessibility.name: The block is a group named by `fileName`, else by `labels.code`; with `files`, the files are tabs of the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern.
accessibility.keyboard: The code scrolls sideways instead of wrapping, and is a tab stop, so the keyboard can scroll it too.
accessibility.copy: The copy button announces the result, and the line numbers, drawn by CSS, are neither read with the code nor copied.

chip.summary: Compact label for an attribute, a status or a filter.
chip.description: A chip with only a label is text; with `onClick` it is a button, with `selected` a toggle, and `onDelete` gives it a separate delete button.

statuses.title: Statuses
statuses.description: Soft chips, one intent per status, with the status written in the label.

filters.title: Filters
filters.description: Selectable chips in a named group: each one is a toggle button.

accessibility.text: A chip without `onClick` is plain text, not a control.
accessibility.toggle: With `onClick` it is a native button; with `selected` it is a toggle with `aria-pressed`, and its check mark is a shape besides the color.
accessibility.remove: The delete button is separate, a tab stop of its own, named by `deleteLabel`, e.g. `Remove Status: open`.

avatar.summary: Picture or initials of a person or an entity.
avatar.description: Shows the image of `src`, or the initials of `name` when there is none or it fails to load. The `name` is also its accessible name, unless `decorative` hides it next to a name already written.

profile.title: Next to the name
profile.description: The name is written beside it, so the avatar is `decorative` and is not read twice.

crew.title: A crew
crew.description: Avatars alone in a list: each one is named by its `name`, and the initials come from its first and last words.

accessibility.name: Without `decorative`, the avatar is an image (`role='img'`) named by `name`; the initials are hidden.
accessibility.decorative: With `decorative` it is hidden from assistive technologies: use it when the name is next to it.
accessibility.image: With `src`, the image takes `name` as its `alt`, or an empty `alt` when decorative.

badge.summary: Count or dot attached to an element, e.g. unread messages.
badge.description: Wraps the element it marks. `content` takes a number or a short text, and numbers above `max` show as `99+`; `dot` shows a dot instead, and `invisible` hides it when there is nothing new.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: A count with a `label` read after the button; the second button already says the count, so its badge is `decorative`.

presence.title: Presence
presence.description: Dots on avatars tell who is online; `invisible` hides the dot of someone offline.

accessibility.label: The visual count is hidden from assistive technologies: `label` states what it means, as hidden text next to the element.
accessibility.decorative: Mark it `decorative` when the element already says it, e.g. an `IconButton` labelled `Alerts, 120 unread`.
accessibility.dot: A dot has no text, so its `label` is the only way to tell what it means.

card.summary: Raised surface grouping related content, with an optional header.
card.description: `CardHeader` gives a title and its subtitle, with room for an avatar before and controls after; `CardContent` holds the rest. `variant='elevated'` adds a shadow for a card over other content.

parts.cardHeader: The title of the card, a heading of `headingLevel`, with its `subtitle`, `avatar` and `action`.
parts.cardContent: The body of the card, in secondary text.

profile.title: A profile
profile.description: A `section` named by its title, with an avatar, an actions button and chips in the content.

articles.title: Entries of a log
articles.description: A list of `article` cards in a `Grid`, each one with its heading one level below the section.

accessibility.region: With `as='section'` or `as='article'`, the card is a region named by the title of its `CardHeader`, or by `aria-label` without one.
accessibility.heading: Pick `headingLevel` from the outline of the page, not from the size: the title looks the same at any level.
accessibility.actions: Links and buttons go in `action` or in the content, never around the whole card.

carousel.summary: Slides shown one at a time, with buttons to move between them.
carousel.description: Each child is a slide. The previous and next buttons and one button per position move between them; `loop` goes from the last to the first. It never moves by itself.

reports.title: Reports
reports.description: Cards as slides, with `loop` so the next button of the last slide goes back to the first.

controlled.title: Controlled
controlled.description: `index` and `onIndexChange` keep the slide in the state of the parent, which shows it and can move it.

accessibility.region: A region named by `label`, announced as a carousel; each slide is a group named by its position, e.g. `2 of 3`.
accessibility.keyboard: The arrow keys move between slides and Home and End go to the ends; the position buttons are a single tab stop.
accessibility.hidden: The hidden slides are `inert`: their content is neither focused nor read.
accessibility.motion: There is no autoplay, and the transition is instant with reduced motion.

divider.summary: Thin line separating groups of content.
divider.description: Horizontal by default, between blocks; `orientation='vertical'` separates the items of a row and stretches to its height.

toolbar.title: Groups of buttons
toolbar.description: A vertical divider between the editing buttons and the others of a row.

sections.title: Sections
sections.description: A separator between the header and the details, and a `decorative` line before a note.

accessibility.separator: It is announced as a separator, vertical ones with `aria-orientation`.
accessibility.decorative: With `decorative` it is hidden from assistive technologies: use it when headings or lists already group the content.
accessibility.contrast: The line is lighter than 3:1, so the grouping never depends on it alone: keep the spacing or the headings.

list.summary: A list of records, one per row, with content before and after each one.
list.description: Each `ListItem` has a title, an optional supporting line, and `leading` and `trailing` content such as an `Avatar`, a value or a `Chip`. `ordered` renders an ordered list.

parts.listItem: A row: its `title` and `description`, between `leading` and `trailing`.

crew.title: Crew
crew.description: Decorative avatars before each name, since the title already says it, and a status chip after.

ranking.title: Ranking
ranking.description: An `ordered` list, whose position is announced; the title writes it too, since the list has no markers.

accessibility.count: A native list, `ul` or `ol`: assistive technologies announce the number of items and the position of each one.
accessibility.controls: Links and buttons go in `title` or `trailing`, never around the whole item.
accessibility.table: For records compared column by column, use a `Table`.

statCard.summary: Key figure of a dashboard: what is measured, its value and how it changed.
statCard.description: `change` gives the variation and its trend, whose color follows the sentiment: a rising cost is `negative`. `description` adds the context, and `loading` shows a placeholder.

indicators.title: Indicators
indicators.description: Three cards in a `Grid`: a rising revenue, a rising cost with `sentiment: 'negative'`, and no change.

loading.title: Loading
loading.description: `loading` replaces the value and the change with a placeholder, and announces that it loads.

accessibility.trend: The trend is told by an arrow and by hidden text, e.g. `Up 12%`, and the sentiment by color: neither rests on color alone.
accessibility.loading: While it loads, the card is `aria-busy` and announces `labels.loading` in place of the value.

skeleton.summary: Placeholder with the shape of content that is still loading.
skeleton.description: `shape` follows what it stands for: a line of `text`, a `rectangle` for a picture or a card, a `circle` for an avatar. Compose several into the layout of the content; for paragraphs and lists, `SkeletonText` and `SkeletonList` already do.

profile.title: A profile
profile.description: A `circle` and two lines of `text` in the place of an avatar and a name, inside a region marked `aria-busy`.

gallery.title: A gallery
gallery.description: A `rectangle` per picture, with a line for its title, in the `Grid` the content will fill.

accessibility.hidden: It is always hidden from assistive technologies: a placeholder has nothing to read.
accessibility.busy: Mark the region that loads with `aria-busy` and a name, so its content is announced once, when it arrives.
accessibility.motion: The pulse is slow, and stops with reduced motion.

skeletonText.summary: Placeholder of a paragraph that is still loading.
skeletonText.description: As many lines as `lines`, the last one shorter. It announces `label` once, so a screen reader hears that the text loads instead of a row of placeholders.

article.title: A log entry
article.description: The placeholder holds the place of the paragraph until it arrives, while the region around it is `aria-busy`.

card.title: Inside a card
card.description: The header is already known, so only the content waits, with two lines.

accessibility.status: A status region (`role='status'`): it announces `label` once, and the lines are hidden.
accessibility.label: Without `label` it announces the `loadingStatus.loading` text of the provider, or `Loading`: say what loads when several things do.
accessibility.replace: Put the content in its place when it arrives, and turn off the `aria-busy` of the region then.

skeletonList.summary: Placeholder of a list that is still loading.
skeletonList.description: As many rows as `items`, each one with two lines of text; `withLeading` adds a circle before each row, as for the `Avatar` of a `ListItem`. Like `SkeletonText`, it announces `label` once.

crew.title: A crew
crew.description: As many rows as the list will have, with `withLeading` for its avatars, replaced by the `List` when it arrives.

compact.title: Inside a card
compact.description: Five rows without a leading circle, for items that have no avatar.

accessibility.status: A status region (`role='status'`): it announces `label` once, and the rows are hidden.
accessibility.label: Without `label` it announces the `loadingStatus.loading` text of the provider, or `Loading`: say what loads when several things do.
accessibility.replace: Put the list in its place when it arrives, and turn off the `aria-busy` of the region then.

emptyState.summary: Tells that there is nothing to show yet, and what to do next.
emptyState.description: A `title`, a `description` and an `action` around a neutral icon: an empty list is not an error. Inside a card or a table its title is a paragraph; `headingLevel` makes it a heading when it fills a whole section.

firstUse.title: First use
firstUse.description: Nothing exists yet, so the action creates the first one; `headingLevel={4}` fits the title into the outline of the page.

search.title: No results
search.description: When a search finds nothing, the title repeats it and the action clears it; a status message announces the count.

accessibility.static: It is static content: it is read where it is, not announced when it appears.
accessibility.heading: Pick `headingLevel` from the outline of the page, and leave it out inside a component that already has a heading.
accessibility.results: When it replaces results, announce the new count with a status message, as `DataTable` does.

errorState.summary: Tells that content could not be loaded, and offers to try again.
errorState.description: `onRetry` shows a retry button, named by `labels.retry`; `action` puts any other action in its place. It announces itself as an alert when it appears, unless `announce` is off.

retry.title: Try again
retry.description: `onRetry` loads again. The first error is on the page from the start, so only the next one is announced, with `announce`.

offline.title: Another action
offline.description: An `action` in place of the retry button, when trying again would not help.

accessibility.alert: With `announce` (the default) it is an alert (`role='alert'`), read as soon as it appears; turn it off when it is on the page from the first render, e.g. rendered by the server.
accessibility.color: The error is told by the icon, the title and the color together: never by color alone.
accessibility.retry: It does not move the focus. The retry button is named by `labels.retry`, translated with the rest of the interface.

table.summary: Native table styled with the tokens, for data in rows and columns.
table.description: Compose it with `TableHead`, `TableBody`, `TableFooter`, `TableRow`, `TableHeaderCell` and `TableCell`. `caption` names it, `density='compact'` tightens it for scanning, and it scrolls sideways when the columns do not fit.

parts.tableFooter: The rows of totals or notes (`tfoot`).
parts.tableHeaderCell: A header cell (`th`): of its column by default, of its row with `scope='row'`; `onSort` makes it a sort button.
parts.tableCell: A data cell (`td`), aligned by `align`: numbers to the `end`.

bounties.title: Rows and a total
bounties.description: The name heads each row (`scope='row'`), the rewards align to the `end`, and a `TableFooter` sums them.

sortable.title: A sortable column
sortable.description: `onSort` and `sortDirection` make a header a sort button, and the parent sorts the rows; `density='compact'` tightens them.

accessibility.caption: `caption` is required: it names the table, also when `hideCaption` hides it under a heading that says the same.
accessibility.headers: Name every column with a `TableHeaderCell`, and each row with one of `scope='row'` when a cell identifies it: screen readers read them with each cell.
accessibility.scroll: When the columns do not fit, the container scrolls sideways and becomes a focusable region named by the caption, so the keyboard scrolls it too.
accessibility.layout: A table is for data compared across rows and columns; for layout, use `Grid` or `Stack`.

dataTable.summary: Table of records with sorting, a text filter and pagination.
dataTable.description: Give it `columns`, `rows` and `getRowId`: each column renders its `cell`, sorts by its `sortValue` and is searched by its `filterValue`. `status` shows the loading and error states; with `processing='server'`, the server sorts, filters and pages, and the table reports the changes.

filter.title: Search and pages
filter.description: A `SearchField` drives `filter`; the rows start sorted by reward with `defaultSort`, five per page.

states.title: States
states.description: `status` shows placeholders or the error state with `onRetry`; `emptyState` replaces the default message when there are no rows.

accessibility.sort: Sortable headers are buttons, and `aria-sort` tells which column orders the rows.
accessibility.announcements: A polite status message announces the new order, the visible rows or the number of results after each change.
accessibility.pagination: The pages are a `Pagination` landmark named from `caption`, and the rows keep their `aria-rowindex` across pages.
accessibility.states: While it loads, the table is `aria-busy`; an error is announced, and an empty table shows an `EmptyState`.

alert.summary: Message about the page or a task, with an optional action.
alert.description: `intent` gives the meaning and picks the icon, `variant` the emphasis. A `title` summarizes the message, `action` adds a related action and `onDismiss` a button that closes it; removing it is up to the parent.

saved.title: Outcome of an action
saved.description: A `success` alert that appears after saving: `announce='polite'` reads it without interrupting, and `onDismiss` closes it.

maintenance.title: With an action
maintenance.description: An `outline` warning, part of the page from the start, with the action that solves it.

accessibility.announce: It is static by default. Use `announce='polite'` for an outcome that appears after an action, and `'assertive'` only for a problem that needs attention now.
accessibility.icon: The icon follows the intent, so success, warning and error differ in shape as well as in color.
accessibility.dismiss: The dismiss button is named by `labels.dismiss`; move the focus somewhere sensible when the alert that had it goes away.

progressBar.summary: Progress of an operation, as a bar or a ring.
progressBar.description: With `value` (between `min` and `max`) it shows how much is done; without it, that something is going on. `valueText` says the value in words when a percentage means little, e.g. `Part 2 of 5`.

upload.title: Known progress
upload.description: The report goes in five parts: `max={5}` and `valueText` tell assistive technologies which part is on its way.

indeterminate.title: Unknown duration
indeterminate.description: Without `value` the bar sweeps and the ring turns; a `small` ring fits next to a line of text.

accessibility.label: `label` names it (`aria-label`) and cannot be blank: say what progresses, e.g. `Sending the bounty report`.
accessibility.value: It is a `progressbar` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`; without `value` they are left out, as ARIA prescribes.
accessibility.motion: With reduced motion, the indeterminate bar pulses in place instead of sweeping.

tooltip.summary: Short supplementary text about a control, shown on hover and focus.
tooltip.description: It wraps one focusable element that already has a name, and adds a description: a keyboard shortcut, the full form of a truncated label. `placement` picks its side and flips when there is no room; `delay` is the hover before it appears.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.description: Each `IconButton` is named by its `label`; the tooltip only adds the shortcut.

truncated.title: Truncated labels
truncated.description: The full name of each ship, cut by an ellipsis; `placement='end'` shows it after the button.

accessibility.describes: It describes its trigger (`aria-describedby`) and never names it: a trigger without a name of its own is reported in the console.
accessibility.content: Plain text only: a tooltip cannot be focused, so a link or a button in it would be out of reach. Use a `Popover` for those.
accessibility.disabled: A disabled control receives no hover or focus, so it never shows its tooltip: explain why it is disabled in visible text.

popover.summary: Panel of interactive content anchored to the button that opens it.
popover.description: It opens from its `trigger` with fields, buttons or links: filters, a short form, details. `title` names it with a visible heading, or `label` without one; `placement` picks its side and flips when there is no room. `open` and `onOpenChange` let the parent control it.

filters.title: Filters with a form
filters.description: The parent owns `open`, so applying the filters closes the popover; `closeOnOutsideClick={false}` keeps the fields when a click lands outside.

details.title: Details without a heading
details.description: `label` names the popover when its text already says what it is about; `placement='bottom-end'` aligns it to the end of its button.

accessibility.dialog: It is a `dialog` named by its `title` or `label`, and its trigger receives `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`.
accessibility.focus: While open it is modal: focus moves into it and stays there, and Escape or a click outside close it and return focus to the trigger.
accessibility.name: For plain text that only describes a control, use a `Tooltip`: a popover is for content the reader acts on.

menu.summary: List of actions opened from a button.
menu.description: `trigger` is the button that opens the menu and names it; `items` are its actions (`MenuItemOption`) and separators (`MenuSeparator`), in order. An item runs its `onSelect` after the menu has closed, so it can open a dialog.

types.menuItemOption: An action of the menu, an entry of `items`.
types.menuSeparator: A line between groups of items, an entry of `items`.

actions.title: Actions of each row
actions.description: Each `IconButton` names its menu after the member it acts on, and the last item is `destructive`.

shortcuts.title: Icons, shortcuts and disabled items
shortcuts.description: Decorative icons, the `shortcut` of each action on the page, and an item `disabled` until there is an entry to paste.

accessibility.name: The trigger names the menu: give an `IconButton` a `label` that says what the actions apply to.
accessibility.keyboard: Enter, Space and Down open it on the first item, Up on the last; the arrow keys, Home, End and typing move between the items, and Escape or Tab close it.
accessibility.select: Selecting an item closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger before `onSelect` runs; a `disabled` item stays visible, and the arrow keys skip it.

contextMenu.summary: Menu of actions on an element, opened with a right click or the keyboard.
contextMenu.description: It replaces the browser context menu on its child: a right click opens it at the pointer, Shift+F10 or the context menu key under the focused element. `label` names it, `items` takes the same entries as a `Menu`, and `disabled` gives the browser menu back.

types.menuItemOption: An action of the menu, an entry of `items`.
types.menuSeparator: A line between groups of items, an entry of `items`.

logs.title: Actions on each card
logs.description: Each card is focusable (`tabIndex={0}`), so the keyboard opens its menu too; the `label` names the log it acts on.

visibleActions.title: The same actions in sight
visibleActions.description: A context menu is hard to discover, so the card also has a `Menu` button with the same items.

accessibility.keyboard: Shift+F10 and the context menu key open it under the focused element; inside, it behaves like a `Menu`, and focus returns to the element on close.
accessibility.focusable: Make its child focusable (`tabIndex={0}`, or a native control): without focus, the keyboard cannot open the menu.
accessibility.discover: Nothing shows that a context menu exists: offer the same actions somewhere visible as well, such as a `Menu` button.

dialog.summary: Modal dialog for a task or a decision that interrupts the page.
dialog.description: The parent owns `open` and closes it in `onClose`, which says what asked to close: `'escape'`, `'outside'` or `'close-button'`. `title` names it, `description` describes it, `actions` go at its end with the main one last, and `size` sets its maximum width.

form.title: A short form
form.description: `initialFocus` starts on the field, the only thing to do in the dialog; Cancel and Escape discard the draft.

details.title: Information only
details.description: There is nothing to lose, so `closeOnOutsideClick` closes it on a click outside too; `size='large'` gives the list room.

accessibility.name: It is a `dialog` with `aria-modal`, named by its `title` and described by its `description`; `role='alertdialog'` is for an urgent message that requires a response.
accessibility.focus: Focus moves into it on open (the panel, or `initialFocus`), Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside, and the page behind is inert and does not scroll.
accessibility.close: Escape and the close button ask to close; focus returns to the element that opened it, or to `finalFocus` when that element no longer exists.

confirmDialog.summary: Asks to confirm an action, stating its consequence, before it happens.
confirmDialog.description: `title` is the question and `description` the consequence. `onConfirm` performs the action and `onCancel` gives up; `intent='error'` marks a destructive action, and `labels` name the buttons after what they do.

destructive.title: A destructive action
destructive.description: `intent='error'` starts focus on the cancel button, and `labels` name both buttons after the action.

pending.title: An action that takes time
pending.description: `onConfirm` returns a promise: while it is pending, the confirm button is busy and the dialog cannot be dismissed.

accessibility.alertdialog: It is an `alertdialog`: it requires a response, so a click outside does not close it, and Escape cancels.
accessibility.focus: Focus starts on the confirm button, or on the cancel button when `intent='error'`, so that Enter alone never destroys anything.
accessibility.labels: Name the buttons after the action (`'Delete entry'`, `'Keep entry'`) instead of the defaults: each one is read without the question.

drawer.summary: Modal panel that slides from an edge of the screen.
drawer.description: For details, filters or a secondary task beside the page. It behaves like a `Dialog`: the parent owns `open` and closes it in `onClose`. `placement` picks the edge (`start` and `end` follow the reading direction) and `size` its width or height.

details.title: Details of a row
details.description: One drawer for the whole list: the button of each member fills it, and `closeOnOutsideClick` closes it on a click outside.

filters.title: Filters from the start edge
filters.description: `placement='start'` opens it beside the list it filters; it holds fields, so a click outside does not close it.

accessibility.dialog: It is a `dialog` with `aria-modal`, named by its `title`: focus moves into it, stays there, and returns to its trigger on close.
accessibility.placement: `start` and `end` follow the reading direction: on a right-to-left page, `end` is the left edge.
accessibility.close: Its header always has a close button, and Escape asks to close through `onClose`: no one depends on a click outside.

container.summary: Centers the content of a page or a section and limits its width.
container.description: Wrap the content of a page in it: `size` limits the line length (`small` for reading and forms, `large` for dashboards) and the side gutters grow with the viewport.

article.title: A text to read
article.description: A `small` container keeps the lines short enough to read, as an `article`.

accessibility.landmark: `as` gives it the element of its role: `main` once per page for its main content, `article` or `section` for a region; name a `section` with `aria-label`.

stack.summary: Lays its children out in a column or a row, with a gap from the spacing scale.
stack.description: The layout of most groups: fields of a form, buttons of a toolbar, items of a list. `direction` and `gap` take one value or one per breakpoint, e.g. `{ compact: 'column', medium: 'row' }`.

header.title: Header of a section
header.description: A column on a phone and a row from `medium` up, with the title and the actions at the ends.

list.title: A list
list.description: `as='ul'` with `li` children keeps the list semantics without bullets or indentation.

accessibility.order: Keep the visual order the order of the code: the reading and focus order follow the code, not the layout.
accessibility.list: With `as='ul'` or `as='ol'`, each child must be an `li`, and the list is announced with its number of items.

grid.summary: Two-dimensional layout: equal columns per breakpoint, or as many columns as fit.
grid.description: `columns` sets the number of equal columns, per breakpoint if needed; `minColumnWidth` instead fits as many columns of that width as the space allows, without media queries.

parts.gridItem: A cell that spans several columns, or the whole row with `span='full'`.

dashboard.title: Panels of a dashboard
dashboard.description: One column on a phone, two on a tablet and four on a laptop, where the first panel spans two.

gallery.title: A gallery
gallery.description: `minColumnWidth` fits the cards to the width; as a list, each `GridItem` is an `li`.

accessibility.order: The reading and focus order follow the code, not the cells: place the items in the order they are read.
accessibility.list: A collection is a list: `as='ul'` with `GridItem as='li'`.
